newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW-French unemployment rises in May.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-French unemployment rises in May.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on French unemployment which rose in May by a seasonally adjusted 32,400 or 1.1 percent to 3,113,500.

The rise in unemployment was unexpected. My forecast was flat. It was a big number and a really bad number. From a political standpoint, it is clearly a number that will put pressure on the government to take quick measures. It is the business cycle which will do the job (of reducing unemployment), but there will be big pressure (on the government) to accelerate its jobs policy.
PHILIPPE BROSSARD, HEAD OF RESEARCH, ABN AMRO FINANCE:
It's very bad news, the second in a row. We had bad consumer spending in May and the increase in unemployment is bad news as it's reversing a nice (downward) trend we've had since last year.
It shows that hopes that growth by itself will help reduce the deficit is still a gamble. Reducing the (public) deficit is going to be painful and will create tension within the government.
With such bad numbers the fiscal policy, which is moving to a more orthodox line, will be rejected even more vocally.

I find it strong, surprisingly strong, I was not expecting such a strong rise. It is very much above what the market was expecting. But the important message is that there has been a declining trend over the last six months which was interrupted today. I do not think it (the rise) should have any impact on the household consumption figure for May or June. There should be no direct link and consumption for the second quarter should be much stronger than for the first.
The figure is in line with the notion that unemployment is at best stabilising. The recent decreases were misleading in the sense that they gave the impression that there was a reverse.

My forecast was 13 percent (ILO rate) by mid-year but I may have to revise that downwards a little now that they (INSEE) have revised the ILO figures, but not because of a change in situation -- purely technically.

What we had always thought was this transfer (of jobless registrations from the ANPE employment agency to the ASSEDIC unemployment benefit agency,being phased in since end-1996) would decrease the number of unemployed.
Not all people who are unemployed get unemployment benefit so that incentive may be a bit less to register with ASSEDIC.
